baseline.conditions: One upstream day plus docking and current allowance.

title: The river keeps two clocks
daily_life: Millmere needs river deliveries while Reedbank crews need paid docking time. The same current that helps one direction slows the other.
timing: 58 km is the inherited route length. Two scheduled days include upstream and docking allowance; the regional 50 km/day rate is a broad planning baseline, not a guarantee against current.
handoff: A boat report names direction, water mark, passengers and berth. Reversing the trip requires a new current and docking assessment; two days is not automatically a return timetable.
story_option: A sealed cargo receipt arrives before its boat. The arrival clerk must distinguish acceptance of a message from arrival of people.
production: A waterline, mooring rope and tired crew make elapsed time visible. Do not use a montage to erase a docking wait that changes the plot.
direction: Listed a-to-b planning reference; reverse passage requires a fresh itinerary.
geometry: Regional endpoints and route length inherited; connecting line is not a surveyed track.
